title: Trace Sieve: field pseudonymizer and audit shield for observability streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, deployable component (Trace Sieve) that sits in our telemetry ingestion pipeline and performs configurable field-level pseudonymization, selective retention enforcement, and an immutable access/audit watermark for traces, metrics labels, and log fields. The goal is to give teams a safe way to capture enriched trace context (user IDs, request metadata) for debugging and SLO analysis while ensuring tenant controls, minimal SLO impact, and a clear audit trail for who accessed full-context data and when.
background: Current observability pipelines capture rich trace attributes and user-identifiable fields that are useful for latency/error dashboards and root-cause analysis. Security and compliance teams require stronger guarantees: (1) field-level pseudonymization for stored telemetry, (2) per-tenant retention policies enforced at ingest, (3) RBAC-gated just-in-time reveal flows with audit logging. Prior tickets built schema-driven scrubbing and tenant-scoped retention but lacked a low-latency, audit-forward shim for trace enrichment. This ticket implements the ingest-side sieve + audit bridge and ties into Console rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Trace Sieve deployed as a stage in the ingestion pipeline that can be toggled per-route and per-tenant
Configurable rules engine supports: field pseudonymization (deterministic), field drop, TTL override for tenant-scoped retention
Just-in-time reveal API: authorized Console sessions can request ephemeral re-identification tokens; every reveal is recorded in an immutable audit log with identity, reason, and trace id
End-to-end latency added by Trace Sieve < 8ms p95 for typical payloads (verified in load test)
Automated unit + integration tests covering rule evaluation, pseudonymization determinism, and audit writes
Documentation in Console explaining per-route toggles, policy precedence, and incident playbook
tasks: Design rules schema and precedence (global -> org -> route -> sample override)
Implement deterministic pseudonymizer with stable salt per-tenant (supports lookup-free matching)
Instrument low-latency path and add metrics: sieve.processing_time_ms, sieve.rules_evaluated, sieve.reveals_requested
Add RBAC checks for reveal endpoint and wire up audit events to Console retention storage
End-to-end load test simulating 10k req/s ingest and 90/10 sampling and measure p95 latency
Create Console UI toggles and rollout plan (canary 3% -> 25% -> 100%)
Security review and threat model signoff before canary
